audit_findings.title: Equity-method stakes may be counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $52.0 million of 2025 affiliate income, equal to 19.7% of the $264.2 million anchor; $338.8 million bridge addition, including $232.4 million of equity-method investments
audit_findings.mechanism: Affiliate earnings may remain in anchor OE and be capitalized through the forecast and terminal value while the investments producing those earnings are also added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Equity in net income of affiliates was $52 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to $50 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that affiliate income and the investments both exist, but the supplied record does not demonstrate whether the OE worksheet removed the income. If it did not, the duplication is reasonably capable of materially overstating value because the annual affiliate income is nearly one-fifth of anchor OE.
audit_findings.action: Trace the OE worksheet for explicit removal of the $52.0 million equity-method income and marketable-security gains or losses, then rerun by either excluding those returns from OE or removing the corresponding investments from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Parent numerator is mixed with consolidated JV cash-flow components
audit_findings.magnitude: $90.3 million of 2025 income attributable to NCI, equal to 34.2% of the $264.2 million anchor; net correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable net income is combined with consolidated depreciation, capital spending and working-capital movements, while value is divided only among Lear common shares; consolidated cash may also include NCI claims.
audit_findings.evidence: Of these joint ventures, eight are consolidated, and ten are accounted for using the equity method of accounting.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim-perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. Its direction cannot be established because removing NCI shares of depreciation and cash reduces value, while removing NCI shares of capital spending and working-capital investment increases it. The $90.3 million NCI earnings scale makes the unresolved net effect reasonably capable of being material.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE component and bridge cash balance on a Lear-parent-attributable basis, or value consolidated equity cash flow and deduct the NCI claim explicitly; rerun all scenarios after reconciliation.

audit_findings.title: All cash appears to be treated as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $1,000.6 million, or $19.32 per diluted share and 20.6% of the $4,851 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds the entire cash balance as a non-operating asset even though some cash may be required for working capital, capital spending, restructuring, debt service or may belong economically to NCI holders.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary liquidity needs are to fund general business requirements, including working capital requirements, capital expenditures, operational restructuring actions and debt service requirements.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the full balance is demonstrated, but the amount that is operating, restricted or attributable to NCI is unresolved. The exposed balance is large enough that a supportable operating-cash reserve could materially reduce the equity bridge and buy threshold.
audit_findings.action: Obtain entity-level cash ownership, restrictions and daily or seasonal liquidity data; estimate minimum operating cash from working-capital and payment-cycle requirements, then rerun the bridge using only verified excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Known 2026 capital-spending increase may be missing from projected OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $98.4 million gross increase from $561.6 million in 2025 to the $660 million 2026 estimate, equal to 37.2% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher maintenance or recurring program capital would reduce projected OE relative to mechanically growing the 2025 anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Capital spending is estimated to be approximately $660 million in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The spending increase is a filed forward estimate, not a demonstrated sustainable reduction in owner earnings. Its valuation relevance depends on how much is maintenance capital, growth or launch investment, and how much is offset by customer tooling reimbursements. First-half 2026 capital spending was $297.3 million, so the full-year outcome also remains prospective.
audit_findings.action: At year-end, reconcile actual 2026 capital spending to maintenance, growth, launch and reimbursable tooling categories; meanwhile run a disclosed sensitivity for the portion of the $98.4 million increase deemed recurring maintenance capital.

audit_findings.title: Latest-year anchor may be distorted by an exceptional restructuring burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $257.1 million of 2025 restructuring and related inefficiency charges, equal to 97.3% of anchor OE; the $253.1 million restructuring total included $46.3 million of asset impairments
audit_findings.mechanism: Leaving nonrecurring or noncash restructuring charges in anchor OE depresses every forecast year and terminal value, while removing recurring footprint-management cash costs would inflate them.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we incurred pretax restructuring costs of $253 million and related manufacturing inefficiency charges of approximately $4 million, as compared to pretax restructuring costs of $139 million and related manufacturing inefficiency charges of approximately $6 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The exceptional 2025 charge level is demonstrated, but the appropriate normalized recurring cash burden is unresolved. Charges were also $138.9 million in 2024 and $132.7 million in 2023, while the first six months of 2026 included $69.0 million of restructuring and approximately $4 million of related charges. That history rules out simply treating the full burden as either permanently recurring or wholly exceptional.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor to employee termination cash costs, contract costs, relocation costs, manufacturing inefficiencies and noncash impairments; establish a recurring cash restructuring allowance and rerun all scenarios with that normalized amount.

audit_findings.title: Nonrecurring tax benefits may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $34.0 million gross 2025 net tax benefit, equal to 12.9% of anchor OE; nonrecurring portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Reserve releases, audit settlements and other one-time tax items could raise anchor OE and then be incorrectly capitalized through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025 and 2024, we recognized net tax benefits of $34 million and $25 million, respectively, related to restructuring charges, the release of tax reserves and audit settlements at foreign subsidiaries, the establishment of a valuation allowance on deferred tax assets of a foreign subsidiary and various other items.
audit_findings.explanation: The $34 million mixed tax benefit is demonstrated, but the filing does not disaggregate the recurring restructuring tax shield from reserve releases, settlements, valuation-allowance effects and other items. Consequently, the record cannot establish the size or materiality of the improper portion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the tax-item rollforward and OE worksheet treatment; retain tax effects associated with recurring costs, remove reserve releases, audit settlements and other nonrecurring benefits, and rerun if the identified adjustment is material.
